the development of mAb reagents for the determination of influenza vaccine potency and identity, and with the use of these mAbs in the development of alternative methods for the determination of vaccine potency and identity.

the mAbs developed and characterized herein are suitable for the development of alternative assays to the SRID assay for the determination of influenza B identity, and for the determination of potency in quadrivalent vaccines.

the use of mAb reagents in the antibody-capture assay format is a promising alternative for the determination of influenza B identity in inactivated influenza vaccines and that the assay can also serve as an alternative for potency determination of influenza B vaccines.

the lineage-specific mAb reagents described here can serve as a useful tool for the development of simple and robust antibody-based identity and potency assays for influenza vaccines containing influenza B virus antigens.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a set of lineage-specific mAbs that can distinguish the two antigenically and genotypically distinct lineages of HA from the two influenza B viruses, and can be used in a variety of applications including identity and potency assays for quadrivalent influenza vaccines.

we have generated and characterized mAbs specific for the HA from two lineages of B viruses, which are useful for setting-up lineage-specific identity tests and for quantifying influenza B HA in inactivated vaccine samples, and that the antibody-capture format of these tests can distinguish heat-stressed from unstressed vaccine.

lineage-specific mAbs can be used in a simple antibody-capture ELISAs to quantify HA in influenza vaccines, and that these assays may have advantages over SRID in terms of speed and cost.
